top_story_title: Exploited Fortinet bug used to plant a stealthy FortiGate implant at a telecom operator
top_story_summary: SecurityWeek reports that an exploited Fortinet vulnerability has been tied to a persistent, stealthy implant deployed on a FortiGate firewall belonging to a telecommunications organisation. The report does not name the CVE, the affected FortiOS branch or a fixed build, so treat the exposure as "any internet-facing FortiGate until proven otherwise" rather than scoping it to a single release.
top_actions: Enumerate every FortiGate, FortiProxy and FortiManager unit from asset inventory with its exact running firmware build, and compare against Fortinet's current advisories - check the vendor advisory for the fixed release, as the report names neither the CVE nor a fixed build.
Remove administrative access (HTTPS/SSH/API) from all internet-facing and untrusted interfaces immediately; restrict management to a dedicated management VLAN or out-of-band network.
Hunt before you patch: review the configuration for unexpected admin users, scripts, static routes, modified login or portal pages, and unexplained outbound connections from the firewall itself.
Upgrade on the vendor's fixed path, HA secondary first, then fail over and upgrade the primary.
After patching, rotate local admin credentials, API keys, certificates and VPN pre-shared keys - a pre-patch compromise survives the upgrade.
executive_summary: An exploited Fortinet vulnerability has been linked to a persistent, stealthy implant on a FortiGate firewall at a telecommunications organisation; no CVE or fixed build is stated, so verify running versions against Fortinet's advisories directly.

An unpatched flaw in Broadcom's Wi-Fi setup software gives an attacker within radio range code execution as root on Broadcom-based routers with no network password and no pairing step; demonstrated against ISP-supplied home gateways, with no fix available.
Attackers are exploiting an OS command injection flaw in SiteGuard Server Edition to run commands as root or SYSTEM on the web servers the WAF is meant to protect.

Two of today's three in-scope items have no stated fixed release - exposure reduction (management plane off untrusted networks, segmentation, credential rotation) is the available control, not patching.
Nothing in this window genuinely concerns AI; no AI section today and no new vendor AI defences in the sources.
key_actions: **Fortinet** — Inventory all FortiGate units with exact running firmware build; prioritise any unit terminating untrusted traffic or exposing administrative services.

**Fortinet** — Confirm the running version against Fortinet's fixed-release table and schedule the upgrade in the change window, HA pair secondary first - check the vendor advisory for the fixed release, as none is stated here.
**Broadcom** — Identify Broadcom-based gateways in scope: ISP-supplied CPE at branch and home-office sites, and any Wi-Fi router carrying corporate remote access.

**Broadcom** — Ask the device maker or ISP for a firmware status on this flaw; when a fixed firmware is published, verify image integrity against the vendor hash before loading - no fixed release is named in the source, so do not assume current firmware is safe.
